title: Past SST predictions add a cloud-linked radiation signal under cubic time controls in five CMIP6 families
abstract: We test timing in published AMIP-minus-HighResMIP radiation differences for 1980-2014. We average seven model pairs into five families. A regression fits past, present and future SST-based Green function predictions, sea ice and cubic time. The past three-month coefficient is 0.650, with a conditional 95% block interval of 0.164-1.112. The all-sky-minus-clear-sky term supplies 0.480 of this point value. The present coefficient is 1.063 (0.681-1.448), and the future coefficient is unresolved. Annual same-year gain stays above one with adjacent-year controls: 2.179 (1.597-2.776). Adding the past term cuts held-out error by 4.66% with cubic controls, but gives no clear gain with linear controls. These exploratory results show an added past, cloud-linked signal under stated controls. They do not identify a response time, prove a causal SST effect, or establish a transferable correction multiplier. Fixed predictors, shared model errors, experiment differences and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Code, input hashes, fit tables, draws and a static figure support reproduction.
